scope: Proposition 9.11 (First-failure propagation) of the manuscript “Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps” (preprints/Metric-measure-limits-of-subcritical-FK-and-spanning-tree-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1dd659698d3a3fde), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 103. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the preceding framework and common- kernel hypotheses, including closure under varying-law extraction with all fixed-offset reference experiments retained as in Proposition 7.11. Assume that the robust lower tests of Proposition 9.5 and the finite catalogue of Proposition 8.28 have been verified for the FK certificate family. Assume also that the strict winding transfer rules of Lemma 9.9 hold at all fixed offsets. Then there are deterministic J, m, R, K and s = p/2 > 0 such that all sufficiently large scales satisfy adjacent ratio bounds in [R−1, R], Aj−m/Aj ≤ 4−sm, and the high-probability lower shell tests. Consequently Equation (9.4) holds.
